title: Operator scripts for LLM canary disaster rehearsal (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working set of operator-facing rehearsal scripts and minimal checklists for simulated LLM canary disasters. Aim: create reliable, repeatable drills that exercise cross-functional handoffs (product, infra, SRE, solutions), telemetry checks, automatic fallback paths, and reversion procedures.

Scope and constraints:
- Focused on inference-canary scenarios (latency spikes, model regression, cache corruption, multi-model routing failures).
- These are NOT full incident runbooks — they are rehearsal scripts oriented toward a 30–60 minute tabletop + live-fire run.
- Keep blast radius small: use micro-slices, synthetic cohorts, and forced-sample traffic only.

Roles during rehearsal (recommended small roster):
- Rehearsal Director (RD) — owns timeline, injects failures, prompts the narrative.
- Operator — runs Redwood Console actions (traffic slices, model route changes, toggles).
- Oncall SRE — validates infra, capacity, scaling, and traces.
- Product/PM steward — speaks to user impact, decides rollout/rollback.
- Solutions/SE — checks customer-facing commitments and private deployment constraints.
- Communications (comms) — posts updates to #rollouts and notifies stakeholders.

Pre-rehearsal checklist (15–20 min before start):
- Confirm micro-slice defined: tag synthetic cohort id=toast-test-<date>.
- Lock canary percent to 1% (or 0.1% for high-risk features).
- Prepare synthetic traffic generator endpoints and scripts.
- Ensure observability dashboards are pinned: latency p50/p95, error rate, model-quality score, token-cost delta, routing fallback count.
- Notify oncall rotation and ensure Pager duty contacts available.
- Snapshot current model version and KV cache state.

Script A: Latency cascade (toy scenario to test throttles + fallback) — 30 min
Goal: validate detection -> graceful fallback to cheaper/older model variant -> rollback path.
Steps:
1) RD: announce start, set timer 00:30.
2) Operator: confirm synthetic cohort receiving 1% traffic.
3) RD: inject artificial latency on model variant A (simulate with traffic generator adding 700ms latency header or toggle in testbed).
4) Operator: watch telemetry — p95 latency should breach SLO in <2m.
5) Operator action checklist (try these in order):
   - Toggle model variant A to canary reserve (pin to safety pool) using Redwood Console route override. Command: (Console -> Routes -> override -> variant A -> set drained=true).
   - If draining not available, reduce slice weight to 0.2% via slice slider.
   - Enable fallback routing policy to variant B (lower-cost quantized model). Use policy: latency-first, max-added-cost 20%.
6) SRE: confirm worker autoscale behaved; check GPU utilization and queue backlog.
7) Product: confirm user-visible latency metrics in synthetic checks. If fallback preserves UX, keep fallback for 15 minutes; else rollback to previous stable model.
8) Post-check: Operator restores original routing and records timings.

Script B: Model-quality regression (hooks into eval alerts) — 45 min
Goal: exercise eval-triggered partial rollback and A/B data collection for postmortem.
Steps:
1) RD: begin, announce measurement windows and label logs with rehearsal_id.
2) Inject regression by patching prompt preprocessor (or use synthetic dataset where model outputs intentionally degrade).
3) Observability should surface quality drop: BLEU/ROUGE-like surrogate, hallucination score, and customer feedback rate.
4) Operator: reduce canary exposure to 0.1% and open gate to human-review flow.
5) Product: decide whether to 1) stop rollout, 2) patch prompt, 3) revert the model.
6) If revert chosen: Operator executes model revert (Console -> Model Catalog -> rollback -> confirm) and updates release notes.
7) SE: validate private-deployments customers have matching rollback applied and that KMS/HSM logs exist.

Script C: KV cache corruption (fast rollback path) — 20 min
Goal: test KV cache flush procedures and replay-safe fallbacks.
Steps:
1) RD: simulate cache corruption by toggling test flag that invalidates prefix cache for the synthetic cohort.
2) Operator: observe token-level cost spike and increased recompute.
3) Quick-mitigations:
   - Toggle per-route cache bypass to true for affected route. (Console -> Routes -> caching -> bypass toggle)
   - Scale up serving replicas for the affected model to absorb recompute pressure (if within budget).
   - If mitigation insufficient, route cohort to stateless variant (route weight swap).
4) Post step: plan cache rebuild and schedule background compaction. Record TTLs and last-successful-checkpoint in runbook.

Communication templates (copyable):
- Initial update (post injection): "Rehearsal RD: Injected latency scenario for canary id toast-test-2024-11-20. Small cohort affected (1%). Operators are validating fallback. Expect update in 5m."
- Escalation (if rollback): "Oncall SRE: Rolling back canary -> stable-2024.10. Snapshot id saved. ETA for full reversion 10m. Notifying customers as required."

Telemetry queries (quick hits):
- p95 latency: telemetry.query('routes.canary.toast-test.p95', last_5m)
- fallback_count: telemetry.query('routing.fallbacks.count', last_15m)
- model_quality: telemetry.query('evals.model_delta.quality_score', last_60m)
- synthetic_success: synthetic.check('toast-test-2024-11-20', pass_rate_threshold=0.95)
Post-rehearsal deliverables (owner: RD & Product):
- 1-page scorecard: what triggered, operator actions, time-to-fallback, user-impact estimate, lessons learned.
- Action items: tickets for automation gaps (example: automated fallback if p95>300ms for 3m).
- Short retro meeting (30m) within 24h with SRE, Product, SE, and at least one operator.

Automations to prioritize after a few rehearsals:
- One-click canary drain button that atomically shifts slice weight + enables fallback policy + opens human-review channel.
- Synthetic-scheduler to run smoke checks automatically on every canary increment.
- Auto-annotate timeline in incident timeline with rehearsal_id and action tags.

Open questions and follow-ups (note-to-self):
- How do we test multi-model routing oscillations without triggering global balancing heuristics? (target: dev-only orchestration layer)
- Define safe thresholds for private deployments (customer contracts may require manual approvals).
- Consolidate telemetry lexicon: unify "model-quality" across eval infra and product dashboards.

Appendix: quick operator cheat sheet
- Drain a canary variant: Console -> Models -> Variant -> Actions -> Drain -> confirm
- Shift traffic slice weight: Console -> Routes -> Slices -> select -> set percentage -> save
- Enable fallback policy: Console -> Routing -> Policies -> select -> set mode=latency-first -> enable
- Revert to stable model: Console -> Model Catalog -> choose stable -> rollback -> confirm -> annotate

Notes: Keep scripts short and action-oriented. The goal is confidence: teams should be able to perform a safe rollback or fallback within 10 minutes of detection for small-batch canaries.

Last edited by Ava Chen on 2024-11-20. Work in progress — please add run times, owners for each subtask, and test data ids.
